subject: Renewal + Capacity increase — order form and MSA terms
messages:
From: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@acme-cloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Cloud Procurement <procurement@acme-cloud.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal window + add capacity — initial details

Hi Karthik,

Quick note — our existing agreement is up for renewal on 2027-08-15. We're planning to renew for 24 months but need to increase committed capacity by ~40% (see attached PO). Procurement asked us to get legal redlines on the MSA and confirm pricing on the new SKUs.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm updated per-token pricing for the higher committed tier (SKU: RU-HIGH-40)
- Add clarification on data residency for EU-sourced traffic (we must maintain EU data at rest in EU)
- Confirm whether Redwood can support scheduled capacity ramp (2-week ramp with burst for migration)

Attaching the PO and a short order summary. Can we get a legal contact and rough timeline for final docs?

Attachments: ACME_PO_Q3_2027.pdf (purchase order, 2 pages)

Thanks,
Natalie Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
ACME Cloud
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + add capacity — initial details

Hi Natalie — thanks for the PO and the heads up.

Looping in Rishi (Legal) and Laura (Customer Success) to handle the contract/ops pieces. High level: we can support a 24-month renewal and the 2-week ramp with burst capacity, but I need legal to confirm the MSA language on data residency and the liability cap for expanded committed usage.

Rishi / Laura — Natalie included a proposed PO and mentioned a ~40% committed increase. Can legal review MSA redlines and confirm what language we'd need for an EU data residency addendum? Laura — can you draft a brief ramp plan we can attach to the order form?

Proposed next steps:
- Rishi: send redlines to ACME by EOD tomorrow
- Laura: share ramp + ops checklist by Thursday
- Natalie: let us know target signature date (ACME) — is 2027-08-10 feasible?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal window + add capacity — initial details

Hi Natalie — thanks, I've reviewed the PO and the baseline MSA. I've attached tracked-change redlines to both the MSA and the order form. Summary of material points:

1) Data residency: your ask to keep EU-sourced data at rest in the EU is reasonable. We can't change the base MSA to a blanket geographic restriction, but we can add a targeted Addendum (Data Residency Addendum) that commits EU at-rest storage to EU region for EU-designated tenants. I've proposed clause language in redline_msa_2027.docx.

2) Liability cap: the existing MSA cap is tied to fees in the prior year. For this renewal with larger committed spend, we propose to keep cap at 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months. ACME requested uncapped liability for certain regulatory fines — we cannot accept that; I've proposed a carveout limited to gross negligence / willful misconduct.

3) SLA/Capacity burst: I added language for a one-time scheduled burst (up to 2x committed capacity for up to 72 hours) and a ramp schedule requirement (customer provides 10-business-day notice for sustained increases beyond the burst window). Ops to confirm feasibility.

4) Confidentiality / Audit: added clearer audit window and encryption obligations to match enterprise controls requested.

Please see attached for tracked changes (redline_msa_2027.docx, redline_orderform_2027.docx). I flagged a few items where we need ACME's procurement/legal to confirm.

Attachments: redline_msa_2027.docx (MSA tracked changes), redline_orderform_2027.docx (order form tracked)

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@acme-cloud.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Cloud Procurement <procurement@acme-cloud.com>, ACME Legal <legal@acme-cloud.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal window + add capacity — initial details

Thanks Rishi — and thanks Karthik. I reviewed the redlines with our legal and procurement teams. A few follow-ups from our side:

- Data Residency: ACME prefers an explicit clause in the MSA (not an addendum) that states EU at-rest data will remain in EU for EU-designated accounts. Can you share why Redwood prefers a separate addendum?
- Liability cap: procurement pushed back on 2x prior fees and requested a fixed cap equal to 6 months of committed fees. Is Redwood able to accept a fixed cap?
- Pricing: attached v3 of the order form with updated SKUs and forecasted monthly usage. Can you confirm the per-unit rates listed for RU-HIGH-40 and the effective start date for the higher committed tier?

Attachment: acme_orderform_v3.xlsx (order form with SKU/pricing tab)

If we can resolve the data residency clause and pricing by Friday, procurement is prepared to circulate for signature next week.

Best,
Natalie Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
ACME Cloud
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@acme-cloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-22T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + add capacity — initial details

Hi Natalie — happy to confirm ops can support the requested ramp plan. Summary of operational commitments we will include in the order form appendix:

- Migration ramp: 2-week scheduled ramp from baseline to new committed capacity, with daily check-ins during cutover.
- One-time burst allowance: up to 72 hours at up to 2x committed capacity to accommodate migration.
- Support: Priority onboarding channel for 30 days post-migration, plus one Technical Account Manager (TAM) assigned.

Regarding pricing, Karthik — if legal can close on the MSA language (Rishi's redlines), we are prepared to honor the RU-HIGH-40 per-unit rate in acme_orderform_v3.xlsx effective on the renewal start date (2027-08-15) provided the signed order reflects the revised committed volume. I'll add the ops appendix and return a final order form for signature once pricing/legal are approved.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-2027-ACME-003

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@acme-cloud.com>, ACME Cloud Procurement <procurement@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-22T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal window + add capacity — order form and MSA terms (final)

Hi Natalie & team — appreciate the quick turn. After internal discussion:

1) Data residency: we will accept an explicit Data Residency clause inserted into the MSA (Section 6.4 in redline) that commits EU at-rest data to EU regions for EU-designated accounts. We had proposed an addendum for modularity, but inserting the clause directly is acceptable for this renewal.

2) Liability cap: we cannot agree to a fixed 6-months-of-fees cap. Our standard compromise for larger commitments is a fixed cap equal to 2x the annual committed fees for the initial 12 months post-signature. If ACME prefers a fixed-number alternative, we can discuss a negotiated flat cap via a commercial amendment (we typically require risk commensurate with committed spend).

3) Pricing & effective date: we confirm the RU-HIGH-40 per-unit rates as shown in acme_orderform_v3.xlsx and will set the effective start date to 2027-08-15, provided the final signed order form reflects the committed quantities.

4) Final steps:
- Rishi: attached is the final MSA + order form with the inserted Data Residency clause and the SLA/ops appendix.
- Laura: will attach the ops appendix to the order form and produce final order form PDF.
- Natalie: once ACME confirms liability language (accept 2x annual fees) we will prepare DocuSign packet for signature.

I've attached the final order form for signature (final_orderform_for_signature.pdf). Please confirm acceptance of the liability position by end of day tomorrow so procurement can circulate. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Attachments: final_orderform_for_signature.pdf

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference
